title: Antikçağda Kadın Olmak
author: Asuman Kafaoğlu-Büke
description: For thousands of years, mythology and art history have portrayed women through the fears, desires and rigid conventions of the male gaze as seductive sinners, destructive sorceresses or silent figures confined to the margins. In Being a Woman in Antiquity, Asuman Kafaoğlu-Büke turns her attention to these overshadowed voices, stripping mythology’s female protagonists of the labels imposed on them by patriarchal civilisations. From Eve and Medea to Penelope, Helen and Venus, she revisits familiar myths to reveal complex, vivid women shaped by their flaws, anger, passions and broken hearts. Insightful and liberating, the book challenges centuries-old stereotypes and invites readers to reconsider some of humanity’s most enduring legends from a fresh, female-centred perspective.
